items.title: Numbers
lines: Life path. Write the birth date as day, month and year. Reduce each of the three separately by adding its digits until one digit is left. Then add the three results and reduce the total the same way. If 11, 22 or 33 appears at any step, keep it and stop. Note: some practitioners instead add every digit of the date at once, which can give a different result.

Expression. Write the full birth name, every first, middle and last name. Give each letter its value from the table (A=1 … I=9, then J=1 again). Add all the values and reduce the total the same way, keeping 11, 22 or 33. Letters are valued A, J, S = 1; B, K, T = 2; C, L, U = 3; D, M, V = 4; E, N, W = 5; F, O, X = 6; G, P, Y = 7; H, Q, Z = 8; I, R = 9.
Reducing. Add the digits of a number together, and repeat until a single digit from 1 to 9 remains. Example: 38 → 3+8 = 11 (a master number, kept); 47 → 4+7 = 11 (kept); 59 → 5+9 = 14 → 1+4 = 5.
Master numbers. 11, 22 and 33 are master numbers. When one of them appears at any step of the reduction, keep it as it is and do not reduce it further.
1 · The First Flame: You are the lamp lit before the others. One flame, one name, one step into the dark. No one walks it for you. Begin, and the room learns your shape.
2 · Two Heartbeats: You were made of two. A hand, and the hand it reaches for. Chest against chest, a breath answering a breath. You know no dance was ever meant for one body.

3 · The Open Mouth: Words come to you at night and want out. Ink, voice, a song held under the tongue. What you swallow still hums behind your teeth. Let it speak. The page is strong enough to carry it.

4 · Stone and Beam: You are the beam that holds the roof. Brick by brick, night by night, you build what stays. Others pass through. You keep the walls standing. Even the dark needs somewhere to live.
5 · The Open Door: No room keeps you long. You hear the road through the wall, and your feet already know it. Change is the only floor you trust. Go. But leave a lamp burning in the window.

6 · The Hand at the Back: You hold others the way a dancer holds a partner: close, careful, steady when the floor tilts. Love is a duty you never asked to be released from. Your arms remember everyone they have held.

7 · The Desk at Night: You are the one still awake when the house sleeps. A lamp, a desk, a question that will not close. You go inward the way others go out. The silence there is yours, and it answers slowly.
8 · Iron in the Hand: You were given weight, and the shoulders to carry it. Power sits in you like iron in a closed hand. Open it gently. Heavy things land hard. What you hold, you hold for real.

9 · The Last Note: You know how a song ends before the first note is sung. Endings find you, and you close them with care, then carry what was learned into the next room. What finishes in your hands is whole.

11 · The Lit Window: You see by a light others cannot find. Signs in the dark. A voice at the edge of hearing. It is not always kind to see this much. Keep the window lit. Someone is walking toward it.

22 · The Builder in the Dark: You build what outlasts the night. Old signs cut into new stone, a house for what had no house. Your hands are slow because what they make must stay. The walls go up around a dream, and the dream stands.

33 · The Open Hand: Your heart was made wide on purpose. You carry other people's sorrow as if it weighed nothing. Every gift costs you something. You give it anyway. Keep one small light for yourself. It is allowed.

items.title: The Journal
lines: You taught me numbers that mean doors, and words no one alive still speaks. I hid them in the songs, where you told me to.
Not all of it. Some of it is only a man asking for one dance.
There is breath on the window this morning. Not mine. Someone wrote a rhyme in it, backwards, from the other side.
By noon it was gone, and I was one day older. She was not.
She has never told me her name. I have stopped asking.
Some nights the page answers before I've finished the line, and I write down what she says as if it were mine.

items.title: The Wood Keeps Answering
lines: Fumus in trabe; nox in veste.
Smoke in the roof beam; night in my clothes.
De viis voces ad lignum porto.
I carry voices from the roads to the wood.
In cute voces, in vase atramentum.
Voices in the skin, ink in the pot.
Sub acu nullum os alienum cantat.
Under the needle no stranger's mouth sings.
This seat alone stands open to me.
Around the fire our place stands empty.
Rubra saltatio transit; pes meus manet.
The red dance passes; my foot stays.
Ignis exstinguitur; nomen meum foris sonat.
The fire goes out; my name sounds outside.

Marseille card XVIII La Lune (The Moon): La Lune's dogs call up into the night and the night calls back, like the wood that keeps answering.

items.title: Ante Acum
lines: Ante horam venio; gelu in veste manet.
I come before the hour; frost stays in my clothes.
Voices from the roads sit with me.
Ante acum iam pateo; cutis adhuc integra.
Before the needle I already lie open; the skin is still whole.
Sedes vacat; in pavimento pedes figo.
The seat is empty; I plant my feet on the floor.
Ante te vēnimus; adhuc nos audis.
We came before you; you still hear us.
The ink is ready: the shield not yet written.
No needle yet; already no covering.

items.title: Sub Lucerna
lines: Lucerna descendit; umbra ad cubitum cadit.
The lamp comes down; the shadow falls to the elbow.
I lay down my arm. I offer bare skin.
In patina ferrum; in vase atramentum.
Iron in the dish; ink in the pot.
Pollex cutem tendit; umbra non tremit.
The thumb stretches the skin; the shadow does not tremble.
Before the touch: voices under the tongue.
The needle touches for the first time.
Mouths without a body are shut.
Usque ad brachium te secuti sumus.
We followed you as far as the arm.
Here you no longer hear us.
The lamp stays; my shadow, alone.
Number 8: Sub Lucerna sums to 35, which reduces to 8: weight, one hand under the lamp and the first touch of the needle.
Marseille card VIIII L'Hermite (The Hermit): L'Hermite holds up his lantern; under one lamp, one hand, the work begins.

items.title: Caelum Non Respondet
lines: Ad sacerdotem venio; manus vacuas ostendo.
I come to the priest; I show empty hands.
Digitum ad caelum tollo; nihil descendit.
I lift a finger to the sky; nothing comes down.
Then I point to the tree outside the door.
The branch bends in the wind; the priest is silent.
A rope pulled taut to the bell.
The tree moves. The sky does not answer.
Number 7: Caelum Non Respondet sums to 79, which reduces to 7: solitude and inner search, a question lifted to a sky that stays silent.
Marseille card XVII L'Étoile (The Star): L'Étoile kneels under silent stars while a bird sits in the tree: the answer moves in the branch, not the sky.

items.title: Signa Corporis
lines: Inter duo signa cutis nuda restat.
Between two marks bare skin remains.
The line grows; the space becomes a threshold.
What is painted/written… what is painted/written…
Voces de viis in lineas pono.
I set voices from the roads into lines.
Not beyond the edge of the ink.
Before the line we knew your names.
Now we wait at the edge.
The nail stops at bare skin.
The line is closed; the night stays outside.
Number 1: Signa Corporis sums to 73, which reduces to 1: the self, a body that begins to be its own between two marks.
Marseille card VIII La Justice (Justice): La Justice draws the edge with her sword; the line is closed and the night stays outside.

items.title: Ala Sub Cute
lines: In collo ala; in ore spiritus.
A wing on the neck; breath in the mouth.
The nostrils breathe; the lips are silent.
Non aperitur ala; sub cute plicatur.
The wing does not open; it is folded under the skin.
The voice does not come out.
The wing does not come out.
Quis loquitur, si os meum clausum est?
Who is speaking, if my mouth is shut?
The wing is mine; the sky is not mine.
Number 6: Ala Sub Cute sums to 24, which reduces to 6: care, a wing kept folded and safe under the skin.
Marseille card XIIII Tempérance (Temperance): Tempérance has wings and never uses them to leave; the wing under the skin stays.

items.title: Ultrafin
lines: Beyond the weight. Beyond the clasp.
Cinistenax — ash still grips what breath could not clean.
The ash still grips what breath could not clean.
אֵפֶר under the tongue. cinis in the mouth.
Ash under the tongue. Ash in the mouth.

Dirt quiet behind me. Wire empty. Glass locked somewhere.

and leave the soft lie outside where Extradox already put it.
and leave the soft lie outside, where the outside-belief already put it.

items.title: Phlebotenax
lines: מַכָּה — the blow that does not close.
Makkah — the blow that does not close.
Past ash. Past quiet dirt. Past ending weight.
hiatus wide enough for the dance to drink.

if the blood stops, the law dies with her and me.

items.title: Medullifax
lines: Vein open. Shell split. Now deeper —
Ossicruor — bone-gore feeding the dance from inside.
Bone-gore feeding the dance from inside.
Profundsect — deep cut held open past the husk,
A deep cut held open past the husk,
past the breach, into what keeps me standing wrong.

Keep the deep cut from closing.

items.title: Solumrupt
lines: נְפִילָה — the fall that does not soften.
Nefilah — the fall that does not soften.
Marrow already cracked. Now the ground goes.
lapsus through the shell, the vein, the bone, into ruin.
A fall through the shell, the vein, the bone, into ruin.
Floor under the tongue gives way.
No soft god catches the fall.
Cadentifax — falling fracture that will not rise clean.
A falling fracture that will not rise clean.
I go down with the dance still drinking.
No shop. No soft word. No two lights.

items.title: Iugulifax
lines: צַוָּאר — neck that will not close soft.
Tsavvar — a neck that will not close soft.
Floor already split. Now the collar.
Iugulum — the throat, the place of the knife —
Collumsect — cut through the hinge where the song rose.
A cut through the hinge where the song rose.
I sing through the wound now.
No soft god stitches the throat.
Collumsect — cut through, no return stitch.
Cut through, no stitch to bring it back.
I still sing, and the singing bleeds.
Breath whistles out the side of me.
The dance drinks at the collar, never full.
No Amen. No bandage. No clean breath.
Шия — only as seal. Рана — only as seal.
Neck — only as seal. Wound — only as seal.
Тримай — hold the open throat — and pour.
Hold — hold the open throat — and pour.
(Joik dies last wordless. Beds hold. Silence.)

Marseille card XI La Force (Strength): La Force holds the open jaw with bare hands; the song comes out through the open throat.

items.title: Cordifract
lines: לֵב — heart that will not feed the dance.
Lev — a heart that will not feed the dance.
Throat already open. Now the chest.
Pulsanex — pulse that will not feed.
A pulse that will not feed.
חָזֶה — breast opened to the cold.
Ḥazeh — a breast opened to the cold.
σφυγμός fails late. καρδία answers wrong.
The pulse fails late. The heart answers wrong.
Count the beats. Lose the count.
Something sits inside the chest and eats.
No soft god holds the pulse.
Pulsanex — the beat that will not feed.
The beat that will not feed.
It stops, and the dance still steps on it.
One beat. Then the long gap. Then a stumble.
Red fills the hollow where the breath used to turn.
cor. pectus. לֵב. חָזֶה. σφυγμός. καρδία.
Heart. Chest. Heart. Breast. Pulse. Heart.
No Amen. No mending. No second rhythm.

items.title: Sepulcrux
lines: קֶבֶר — grave that will not open for return.
Qever — a grave that will not open for return.
No pulse left to feed. No throat left to sing it.
sepulcrum — tomb laid on the chest —
Sepulcrum — a tomb laid on the chest —
בּוֹר — the pit. τάφος — the tomb. βάρος — the weight.
Bor — the pit. Taphos — the tomb. Baros — the weight.
No soft god raises the sealed.
Tumulifrax — mound fracture shut on me.
A mound fracture shut on me.
No rise. No morning. Only hold.
The dance walks the mound and leaves no footprint that lasts.
It took everything and calls the pit a floor.
sepulcrum. tumulus. קֶבֶר. בּוֹר. τάφος. βάρος.
Tomb. Burial mound. Grave. Pit. Tomb. Weight.
No Amen. No rising. No return.

Grief — only as seal. Sorrow — only as seal.

Marseille card XIII (the nameless arcanum): The nameless arcanum leaves a cleared black field behind it, a ground that is sealed and does not reopen.

items.title: Madreliqu
lines: שְׁאֵרִית — remnant that will not stay buried.
She'erit — a remnant that will not stay buried.
Grave sealed. Mound shut. Under it — wet.

A remnant that will not stay buried.
λείψανον wet. לַח under the seal.
The remnant, wet. Moisture under the seal.
ὑγρός in the dark that Irredanex denied.
Wet in the dark that the no-return denied.

Bibitenax keeps the mouth open under earth.
Ever-drinking keeps the mouth open under the earth.
I sealed the grave and it drank me anyway.
No rise. No return. Only the wet that stays.
The dance finds the moisture under the weight.
umor. reliquiae. שְׁאֵרִית. לַח. λείψανον. ὑγρός.
Moisture. Remains. Remnant. Moist. Relic. Wet.
No Amen. No dry. No clean burial.

Neck — only as seal. Torment — only as seal.

(Joik dies last wordless. Beds hold. Silence.)

items.title: Mendaclox
lines: The lie sealed as empty hold.
Wet relic still drinking. Now name the soft god.
Ultisect — last cut that keeps cutting —
The last cut that keeps cutting —
vanum under the soft word. רִיק where the hold was.
Emptiness under the soft word. Emptiness where the hold was.

The last cut that keeps cutting.

items.title: Praestigiator
lines: A cup, a coin, a knife, a thread,
a tooth he pulled from someone dead.
He sets them out on velvet black,
and none of them is coming back.
His fingers stink of oil and brass.
He winds the key till the spring bites back,
a thin little song through a hairline crack.
The spring is tight, the lid is up,
the dancer bows inside the cup.
He palms the light. He hides the door.
He's done this act a thousand times before.
The crowd is dust. The crowd is bone.
He bows to them like they're his own.
Wind her once, she dances twice,
smiles like the knife was nice.
Number 5: Praestigiator sums to 68, which reduces to 5: change, the sleight of hand that makes things vanish.
Marseille card I Le Bateleur (The Magician): The Conjurer is Le Bateleur, card I, at his table of cups, coins and a knife.

items.title: Temperantia
lines: Not a drop on the floor.
Two cups of glass, one full, one bare,
a wing of ash above the chair.
She tips the light from lip to lip,
and not one note is let to slip.
I drank it once. It tasted of rust,
a song poured slow through a sieve of dust.
She told me wait. She told me breathe.
The note went over. I stayed beneath.
Box to box she carries the thread,
from the living lid to the lid of the dead.
Her wings don't move. Her hands don't shake.
She has never once poured a mistake.
Number 5: Temperantia sums to 50, which reduces to 5: change, poured slowly from one vessel to the next.
Marseille card XIIII Tempérance (Temperance): Temperantia is Tempérance, card XIIII, pouring between two cups without spilling a drop.

items.title: Vis
lines: Bare hands on the hinge of the jaw,
white wrist in the wet of the maw.
I don't pull. I don't pray.
I just stand where the teeth have to stay.
I was the hunger under the stage,
the breath that rattled every cage.
She came in slippers, neck like a swan,
and laid two fingers where the roar comes from.
hold the beast by the bite,
in the mouth of the night.
I tasted her pulse and I let it be,
the only throat I never breached.
She didn't win. She didn't tame.
She held. And holding has no name.

Marseille card XI La Force (Strength): Vis is La Force, card XI in the Marseille order: a woman's hands on the lion's jaw.

lines: One foot tied to the beam of the ceiling,
the other bent like a dancer kneeling.
Coins fall out of his pockets like teeth.
The sky is a floor. The floor is beneath.
Blood in my face, the room turned round,

Every step she takes is over my head,
or under. I can't tell. I'm not quite dead.

through a crack in the lid and the teeth of the locks.

of a grave in the sky,

shine on me. Don't ask why.

items.title: Turris
lines: Count the floors. Then forget them.

a stair for each song and a lock for each trick.
At the top was a crown and a window of glass,
and a girl in pink who was told not to pass.
I stood at the summit and called it my own,

items.title: Mundus
lines: A wreath of black laurel, an oval of thorn,
I dance in the middle where nothing is born.
An ox and a lion, an eagle, a man,
four faces watching me finish the plan.
I gave her the world and the world was a room,
the size of a jewel box, the shape of a tomb.
Every road I walked ended under her feet,
every song I sang came back complete.
I hold it all in one turn,
the whole world, and you are gone.
Four winds came in and they laid themselves down,
the ox gave his back and the lion his crown.

lines: No number. No floor. No fear.

items.title: The Drawer of Tracings
lines: There is a drawer beneath my counter no one opens
Thin sheets of paper, every line a man once wore
I traced them first in pencil, then I laid them on the living
And kept the ghost of each one folded in the dark
I never asked what happened to the drawing
I thought it went with me when I walked out
But some of me stayed flat inside her keeping
A shape of who I was before the work began
The shape stays. The man walks out.
At night I lift them to the window one by one
The bells across the city counting what I hold
A sailor's swallow, someone's mother's handwriting
A wolf for a boy who never learned to be afraid
I wake in a far town and feel a pulling in my arm
As if a page were turning somewhere I cannot see
I am the copy walking, and the first of me is lying
Pressed in her drawer with all the other men
No one comes back the way he left.
They come back months or years from now and lie down quiet
They want the old place darker, or a new place found
I never tell them I could trace them blind by now
I never tell them half of them is mine
I booked the next one before the last had settled
Not for the picture, for the hour I disappear
It hurts like something turning in the chest and still I need it
Her craft is the only room where I can stand the ache
One day the drawer will hold more than the town does
A paper crowd of everyone who ever came to me
And none of them will know the girl who kept them
Has nothing of her own to lay down on the sheet
I keep what you were when you could not
(I left what I was, and I did not know)

items.title: The Seventh Night of the Mark
lines: The first night it burns like a letter I mailed to myself
I sleep on my side so the sheets will not read it
Under the film the dark and my own red settle as one
Two waters in a ditch that will not ever separate
I sent you home with the work still wet and singing
I told you wash it gently, I told you do not pick
You heard the hum of the street and not one word of mine
A man who walks away still listening for the chair
The third night it itches and starts to talk in my sleep
Names I buried rise up through the skin like a tide through sand
My grandfather's cough, the dog we lost in a summer field
Nobody taught it to speak, but it carries the dead in its mouth
Where are you lying now, with your old skin flaking off
Like paper burned at the edges, curling, grey, and gone
I close my eyes in the shop and you are wandering in them
Barefoot in my dark, and you do not know whose dark it is
The fifth night I would give it back, I would give it all
It sits in my chest like a blade that someone forgot to pull
But by morning I am counting what is bare on me again
There is no peace without the ache, and the ache needs her hand
They call it healing, the week the colour sinks below
It is not healing, it is the mark moving in for good
Every day it takes a little more of the man who came
And leaves the one I made to answer to his name
The seventh night the shine goes dull and the lines lie still
I run my thumb across them and they do not feel like mine
I lie down on the bed the way I lay down in her chair
And wait for a hand that is not coming, in a room with no one there
It has settled, and I have not
(It has settled, it was never meant to stop)

items.title: The Last Open Day
lines: The sign in her window was written by hand
Last open day, on a Thursday in March
I read it three times with my coat still wet
And felt the bare places go cold on my back
I did not write it for the town, I wrote it for my hands
They shake a little now when the evening comes
I wrote it for the ones who wear the only work I sign
So they would know there is no other door
No other hand will add to it.
I could walk across the river to a younger shop
Bright walls and music and a list of names
But my body would refuse a stranger's hand
Like a field that only answers to a single plough
You belong to my line, the way a river keeps its bed
Another hand would only write a lie on what I wrote
I made you so no other craft would ever take
And now I am the reason you will stay unfinished
And the work was never finished.
One last time I lay my weight down where it used to fall
She works slower now, her breath is in my ear
I keep a space beneath my ribs she never reached
And I will carry that empty place like a debt into the ground
Hush, I am closing the last line where it starts to turn
Not ending it, just setting it down where it will stay
You will touch the open space for all your years
And it will ache exactly the way I meant it to
I pull the shutter down and the street goes grey
The bottles on the shelf keep breathing in the draft
Somewhere a man is standing at a closed glass door
With half a story on him and no hand left to tell the rest
I am the unwritten part of what you made
(You are the page I put away, still open)

items.title: The Hour Without Words
lines: There is a moment when the work is done and neither of us moves
The machine is off, the street has gone away
She does not ask me how it feels, I do not ask her what she sees
We sit inside the quiet like two stones inside a stream
I read him in the silence better than in any word
The way his shoulders drop, the way his jaw lets go
Each man is a page that only opens when the talking stops
And his has lines on it I never put there
I feel her reading every year I never said aloud
The boy who hid in cupboards, the father at the door
She turns me slowly in her mind and does not close the book
And I have never been so known, and never been so far
He thinks the quiet is a rest, but it is where I work the hardest
I lift the stories off him one by one and set them down
I do not keep them, I do not give them back
They lie between us on the table like a second skin
We read each other in the quiet.
He read the book and said nothing.
If I spoke now the whole of it would break like thin ice over black water
So I hold my breath until my chest is full of what I cannot name
It aches as if a hand were pressing slowly on my heart
And I would sit inside that pressure for the rest of every night
I hear the thing he almost said, it settles in my throat
I will not answer it, the answer would undo the hour
We read each other to the bottom and we never meet
Two lamps turned to the wall in the same unlit room
Then a door slams somewhere down the hall and the hour is over
She stands, I find my coat, we say the price, the date
Everything that passed between us leaves without a sound
And I walk out still written in a language no one speaks
I said nothing, and you heard all of it
(I heard all of it, and I said nothing)

items.title: The Butterfly on the Nape
lines: She set it where my collar ends and no one sees me looking
Two wings across the back of my neck, spread wide and holding still
I feel it shiver when I turn my head against the pillow
As if it heard the open sky and knows it never will
I drew it with the wings already lifting from the body
Not resting, not asleep, but caught the instant it would go
I gave it every reason in the world to leave him
And then I pinned it with the only black I know
In the train window I can see it ride beside my face
A dark thing pressing at the edge of every glass I pass
At night it beats so faintly that I wake and hold my breath
And for a moment I believe the skin will let it out at last
It will not leave, it was not made for leaving
It was made for wanting to, and that is all it ever does
I put the hunger in the wings and kept the sky out of the colour
So he would carry flight the way a cage remembers birds
It won't fly, and it won't rest.
Fly to the sky… no flight…
Some evenings I stand at the open window with my collar down
And let the cold air find it like a hand that calls it home
It aches beneath the hairline, like a word I cannot finish
And I go back inside with the wings and the ache my own
Every man who leaves my chair walks out with something trying
A bird that will not sing, a ship that never clears the bay
His is the one that hurts me most because it nearly made it
A breath from lifting off, and kept that way
When I am old they will turn me over and they will find it
Still straining at the nape with nowhere left to go
The rest of me will rest and it will not
The last thing in me trying, and the last thing in me slow
Open the window, I am still here
(I closed the sky in you, and left the window clear)
It will stand at the threshold.

items.title: What the Black Covers
lines: There is a name under my forearm I do not say anymore
I was someone when I chose it, and that someone isn't here
I asked her to put the dark over it until it's gone
She said nothing is gone, only covered
I can hide a life, I cannot take it from you
The old lines stay under mine like a floor beneath the sea
You will not see him, but you will carry him
That is the only kind of mercy I can do
I cover who I used to be.
I did not hide my guilt.
How much of a man can be painted over before there is no man
I have covered a father, a city, a promise, a year
Every time I come back there is less of me to cover
You think the black is a door you can close behind you
It is a grave you dig in yourself, and stand in, and stay
I do not bury what you were, I bury you a little
And send the rest of you out into the day
I wanted to be no one, and I almost am
Under the dark there is a boy who still believes his name
I cannot reach him, I can only hold my arm at night
And feel him knocking from the other side of what I became
I hear him too, each time you lie down here
Not loud, not asking, only there
I could have told you what the covering costs
I knew you'd pay it, so I didn't care
When they wash me at the end they'll find a darkness, nothing more
No one will read the names beneath, no one will ask
And I will go into the ground with every life still in me
What am I, under all of it
(What you were, and never will be again)
